must_remember: The net displacement during wave superposition is given by the algebraic sum of individual displacements $y(x,t) = y_1(x,t) + y_2(x,t)$ in a linear medium.
Constructive interference occurs when path difference is $\Delta x = n\lambda$ and phase difference is $\Delta\phi = 2n\pi$.
Destructive interference occurs when path difference is $\Delta x = (2n - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2}$ and phase difference is odd multiples of $\pi$.
Standing waves are formed by the superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions, with nodes at zero displacement and antinodes at maximum displacement.
The beat frequency is given by $f_b = |f_1 - f_2|$, representing the periodic rise and fall of sound intensity.
Energy is conserved during interference and is merely redistributed from minima to maxima.

glossary.meaning: The principle stating that when two or more waves overlap, the net displacement at any point is the sum of the individual displacements.
A point along a standing wave where the displacement is zero and pressure variation is maximum.
A point along a standing wave where the displacement amplitude is maximum and pressure variation is zero.
The frequency at which the loudness of sound rises and falls when two sound waves of slightly different frequencies interfere.
